pick.name: Superhuman Mail
pick.what: Keyboard-first email client with AI triage for Gmail and Outlook
pick.why: Fastest inbox-zero workflow; Grammarly rebranded as Superhuman (Oct 2025) and Mail sits in its paid tiers
pick.free_limits: No free plan includes Mail. On the official plans page Mail appears only in Business and Enterprise; Business is reported at ~$33/user/mo annual or ~$40 monthly in USD (page is geo-priced; secondary sources). Grammarly, Docs and Go are bundled in all plans

best_free.name: Thunderbird
best_free.what: Open-source desktop mail client for multiple accounts
best_free.why: Free, local, multi-account; no AI triage

alts.name: Shortwave
alts.free_limits: 14-day trial; Business $30/seat, Premier $45, Max $120; free tier unclear

alts.name: HEY
alts.what: Opinionated email service with screener and feed
alts.why: Best if you want to leave Gmail/Outlook for a new address
alts.free_limits: 30-day free trial; monthly price not readable on fetched page

candidates.name: Superhuman Mail
candidates.verdict: PICK: best speed and triage; pricey

candidates.name: Gmail / Outlook web + built-in AI
candidates.verdict: Zero-cost baseline; Claude connectors can read Gmail

decision: Superhuman Mail is the best email client for people who live in the inbox, but at roughly $33-40 per user per month (Business tier) it only pays off with high volume. Many founders do fine with Gmail or Outlook plus an AI assistant; Thunderbird is the free multi-account client.
details: Exchange Online EWS retirement affects Thunderbird for Microsoft 365 accounts.

verify.note: Checked against primary sources; wording made neutral during verification.
